hook: Preston moved from running two federal agencies during the 2008 financial crisis to leading Goodwill Industries, where he has directed the organization's push to use AI-enabled training tools to help workers displaced by automation move into new careers, applying crisis-era public administration experience to AI's labor disruption.
name: Steve Preston

quote.text: The jobs of the future will require constant reskilling, and the organizations that succeed will be the ones that make that reskilling accessible to everyone, not just the already advantaged.
quote.context: A recurring theme in Preston's public remarks on Goodwill's workforce mission in the AI era

reading.body:
Steve Preston's career is a direct line from federal crisis management to the labor-side consequences of AI scaling: as CEO of Goodwill Industries International, he is deploying AI-enabled training tools to move workers displaced by automation into new careers.

His timeline shows two distinct acts. From 2006 to 2009 he ran federal agencies, the Small Business Administration through Hurricane Katrina recovery lending and HUD through the foreclosure crisis. From 2013 onward he has led Goodwill, and in the 2020s he directed the expansion of reskilling programs aimed specifically at workers in roles automation is eliminating. The operational logic he carries from one act to the other is crisis response: identify a population under acute economic pressure, mobilize institutional resources, move people through a transition.

The AI connection here is on the demand side of the compute chain, not the supply side. Preston's work is not about building models, acquiring power, or constructing data centers. It sits at the end of that chain, where AI deployment changes what jobs exist and what skills they require. The data shows what he has done and what Goodwill's stated mission is, but it does not cover program scale, outcomes for workers who complete reskilling, or how Goodwill measures whether its AI-enabled tools produce durable employment. Those questions are outside what the sources here can answer.

quick_facts: President and CEO of Goodwill Industries International

Led Goodwill's expansion of AI-enabled job training and workforce reskilling programs

achievements.impact: Led HUD through the depths of the 2008 financial crisis and the onset of the foreclosure crisis.

achievements.impact: Directed federal small-business lending and disaster relief programs, including Hurricane Katrina recovery lending.

achievements.title: President and CEO, Goodwill Industries International
achievements.impact: Leads one of the largest nonprofit workforce-development networks in the U.S., expanding job-training programs as automation reshapes entry-level labor markets.
